config

Where MixOS keeps its files, and how a *.conf.mix file is read.

  • config::path(Dir::Etc | Var | Run | Share) delegates to the shared paths resolver: config, state, runtime and prefix/share respectively. Each root uses environment, then layout.mx, then defaults. The prefix location selects the system or user tier. Dirs::resolve(&Environment) uses an explicit environment snapshot.
  • config::parse / config::parse_file and Value, Map, Error, ErrorKind: the strict crate's strict-data loader, re-exported so a config reader needs one dependency. Typed loading is strict::from_file.

No dependency on the Mix language. Test with cargo test -p config.

Node configuration and TLS

node::NodeConfig reads node.conf.mix, selected by MIXOS_NODE_CONFIG or the resolved config directory. The optional maild section contains typed ports, hostname, storage paths, spam settings, the legacy tls_cert / tls_key pair and tls: { identity: [...], strict_sni: false }. Mail state defaults to path(Dir::Var)/maild/{mail.db,blobs,mds}. Unknown service and mail settings survive typed round trips.

Optional jmap_listen, jmap_upstream, smtp_inbound_listen and smtps_listen fields override the corresponding address helpers. Otherwise the helpers use the node IP and mail ports (8443, 25 and 465 by default). jmap_upstream() uses HTTPS. Missing mail settings remain valid.

node::{TlsConfig,TlsIdentityConfig} are always available. Each identity requires server_name, cert and key; its independent default and no_sni_fallback flags default to false. Enable the optional tls feature for load_tls_config(cert_path, key_path) and tls::sni::{SniCertResolver,TlsIdentity,pick_identity}. The resolver loads PEM pairs and matches names case-insensitively. Unknown SNI uses the default; absent SNI prefers the no-SNI identity then the default. If neither flag is set anywhere, the first identity fills both roles. Strict SNI rejects unknown names and clients which omit SNI. default_identity() remains available for pre-TLS greetings, including in strict mode.

from_conf_mix_str and load_conf_mix_path return config::Error (the strict loader error); node search/load functions retain anyhow::Result. Verify TLS with cargo test -p config --features tls.

The source is libs/config.

Application directories

AppDirs places each application's config, durable state and cache under <config>/apps/<component>, <state>/apps/<component> and <cache>/apps/<component>. Component names cannot escape those roots. resolve_with injects resolver inputs for tests. App-owned filenames stay with their owners. Existing saved data is not moved by resolution.

Atomic directories

atomic::open_directory refuses symlinks in every component. atomic::create_directory uses the same held-descriptor walk and provisions missing components with mode 0700. It validates the entire absolute path before creation, refuses parent traversal and leaves existing permissions unchanged.

Web configuration and ACME policy

node::WebdConfig adds the web listener, vhost, share roots, auxiliary DB and ACME settings to NodeConfig. web_listen() derives the legacy listen address; synthesize_listeners() validates explicit binds and host ownership, retaining the fail-soft disabled-host path. Unknown web settings survive typed node round trips.

resolve_webd_acme() checks per-vhost issuance choices, HTTP-01 readiness and the node-level Let's Encrypt production Subscriber Agreement. Only the policy resolver can mint an AcmeTosAcceptance proof.

Node loading, directory resolution and TLS/SNI use the existing config implementations. Client discovery and connect helpers already live in bus::client_helpers; config remains independent of the Bus client.
